## Context / Problem

Every execution opens its pull request against one branch for the whole platform. `TemporalStarter.start` at `services/orchestration/intake_runtime.py:49` sets `base = self._settings.github_default_base_branch`, and that value reaches the pull request unchanged via `DraftPullRequestInput.base` at `services/orchestration/temporal_workflows/draft_pull_request.py:213` into `PullRequestInput.base` at line 742.

A per-ticket base is already modelled and already dead. `IntakeStart.base` is declared at `services/orchestration/intake_reconciler.py:44`, the only construction site at line 365 never sets it, and the starter overwrites it with the setting regardless.

So work depending on an unmerged change cannot be automated. A ticket whose fix only makes sense on top of another open pull request must target the shared default branch, so its diff either carries the parent change as noise or does not apply. This blocks the pilot against `archive-massgov-pfml`, where the fix for ticket `98b3-e6e7-689f-4ae0` needs the Storybook story added by pull request 14 on branch `joeoakhart/PFMLPB-33758` to be exercised at all.

## Approach

Let a ticket declare its base branch, and honour that declaration at intake.

The declaration travels as a `base:<branch>` label. Labels are the one ticket attribute both sources already normalise to a common shape, so a single parser serves both backends and a client on either declares a stacked base the same way. That is why this beats a rebar-only field or a new setting. A setting is wrong regardless of backend, because the base varies per ticket while a setting is per deployment.

The declaration is an override, so `github_default_base_branch` stays authoritative for every ticket that declares nothing and existing behaviour is unchanged. Repeating one value is a duplicate and resolves to it. Two different values is a conflict with no defensible winner, so the ticket is held rather than resolved by list order.

The failure mode is closed. An empty `base_sha` is not inert. It is the workspace checkout commit at `draft_pull_request.py:426` and the fallback gate commit at line 618, so a mistyped branch would root an execution at no known commit. An unresolvable declared base therefore holds the ticket through the existing unroutable path. Falling back to the default would silently target the wrong branch and produce a pull request whose diff is not the one the ticket asked for.

An absent branch is distinguished from a failed lookup. `remote_head` passes `check=True`, so a transient `git ls-remote` failure keeps propagating as it does today, because the ticket is not at fault and the next pass retries it. Only an empty result, a successful lookup matching no ref, holds the ticket.

## Scope

- `services/orchestration/intake_base.py` is new and holds `declared_base` and `UnresolvableBaseBranch`.
- `services/orchestration/intake_reconciler.py` gains `base_branch` on `IntakeCandidate`, populates it in both adapters, passes it as `IntakeStart.base`, and holds the ticket when the starter reports the base unresolvable. `IntakeStart.base` defaults to `""` rather than `"main"`, so the setting stays the only place the default branch is named.
- `services/orchestration/intake_runtime.py` honours `start.base` when set and raises `UnresolvableBaseBranch` when `remote_head` returns empty.
- `README.md` documents the convention, the override precedence, and the hold behaviour.
- Tests: `tests/unit/test_intake_base.py` is new for label parsing. `tests/unit/test_intake_runtime.py` is amended, because it already exercises `TemporalStarter.start` with `remote_head` monkeypatched and `base` defaulted at lines 40 and 76, so it is both an affected consumer and the home for base-selection tests.

## Grounded assumptions

- The workflow already supports an arbitrary base. `DraftPullRequestInput.base` at `draft_pull_request.py:213` reaches `PullRequestInput.base` at line 742 with no reference to the setting, so only intake selection is missing.
- Both sources expose labels under one key. `services/integration/tickets/rebar_backend.py:97` writes `"labels": list(ticket.get("tags") or [])` and `services/integration/jira/normalize.py:42` writes `"labels": list(self.labels)`, so one parser covers both.
- `IntakeStart.base` has no current effect. Its only construction site is `intake_reconciler.py:365` and it omits `base`, so changing the default from `"main"` to `""` cannot alter any existing execution.
- An unresolved branch yields an empty string, not an error. `remote_head` at `intake_runtime.py:25` returns `proc.stdout.split()[0] if proc.stdout.strip() else ""`, and `git ls-remote` exits 0 for a ref that does not match.
- Holding is the established response to an unroutable ticket, via `_hold` at `intake_reconciler.py:249`.
- A starter exception would otherwise abort the pass. `PostgresSideEffectLedger.run_once` at `services/coordination/idempotency.py:108` does not catch effect exceptions, so `_start` must catch it.
- The pilot branch exists. `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/joeoakhart/PFMLPB-33758` against `archive-massgov-pfml` returns `b0117d05d8`, the head of pull request 14.

## Testing

Happy path: a candidate carrying `base:feature-x` starts a workflow based on `feature-x` at that branch's remote head.

Failure and edge paths, each an acceptance criterion below: no label, an empty value, a prefix-only label such as `baseline`, a duplicate value, two conflicting values, a branch name containing a colon, an unresolvable branch, a second candidate still starting after a hold, and a `git ls-remote` failure propagating rather than holding. The prefix is matched case-sensitively because branch names are.

Live end to end: the pilot ticket for `98b3-e6e7-689f-4ae0` opens a pull request against `archive-massgov-pfml` whose base is `joeoakhart/PFMLPB-33758`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A candidate carrying `base:<branch>` starts a workflow whose `base` is that branch (`tests/unit/test_intake_runtime.py`).
- [ ] That workflow's `base_sha` is resolved from the declared branch (same module).
- [ ] A candidate with no `base:` label starts a workflow whose `base` is `github_default_base_branch` (same module).
- [ ] A declared branch that does not resolve on the remote starts no workflow (reconciler test asserting `IntakeReport.started` is empty).
- [ ] That same ticket is recorded in `IntakeReport.held` with a reason naming the branch (same test).
- [ ] A held ticket does not prevent a second candidate in the same pass from starting (reconciler test with two candidates).
- [ ] An empty declaration such as `base:` falls back to the default branch (`tests/unit/test_intake_base.py`).
- [ ] A label such as `baseline` is not read as a declaration (same module).
- [ ] Repeating `base:x` resolves to `x` (same module).
- [ ] `base:x` together with `base:y` raises rather than selecting either (same module).
- [ ] A declared branch containing a colon is preserved in full (same module).
- [ ] `candidate_from_rebar` populates `base_branch` from labels (reconciler test).
- [ ] `candidate_from_jira` populates `base_branch` from labels (reconciler test).
- [ ] A `git ls-remote` failure propagates instead of holding the ticket (test raising `CalledProcessError` from `remote_head`).
- [ ] [non-codebase] A live run of the pilot ticket for `98b3-e6e7-689f-4ae0` opens a pull request against `archive-massgov-pfml` whose base branch is `joeoakhart/PFMLPB-33758`.
  provenance: environment=local-colima-k3s; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the pilot executes the shipped intake and workflow path against the client repository over the same Temporal path a deployment uses
- [ ] `README.md` names the `base:<branch>` label convention, states that the setting applies when no label is present, and states that an unresolvable declared branch holds the ticket.
- [ ] `ruff check services tests scripts adapters` exits 0.
